To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) A novel series of 2,4-disubstituted quinazolines were identified as potent Hsp90 inhibitors; (2) A novel series, 3,4,5,6-tetrahydropyrimidines, was identified as potent inhibitors of measles virus RNA polymerase; and (3) A novel series 4,5-dihydroisoxazol-4-yl-pyridines was identified as potent angiogenesis inhibitors

(1) the measles virus RNA-dependent polymerase (RdRp) is a promising target for antiviral drug discovery; (2) the Hsp90 is a potential target for anti-tumor drug discovery; and (3) Zebrafish is a promising model for high throughput anti-angiogenesis drug discovery.

(1) the measles virus RNA-dependent-RNA polymerase inhibitors discovered in the HTS campaign are potent inhibitors of measles virus replication in cell culture and are active against the measles virus in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of new drugs for cancer and virus infection.
the discovery of novel small molecules that can serve as probes of biological pathways, as well as potential drug candidates.
the identification of small molecule inhibitors of cancer and viruses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of medicinal chemistry in the context of HTS and SEA has led to the discovery of new classes of compounds with novel modes of action.
HTS and VS are complementary and can be used in a synergistic manner to accelerate the discovery of novel drug leads.
Emory has a unique and successful combination of HTS, medicinal chemistry and VS programs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a multi-disciplinary approach to the identification of novel chemical probes for biological targets.
the combination of HTS and VS has led to the discovery of several new classes of compounds with potent anti-cancer and anti-viral activity.

the integration of HTS, chemical diversity and substructure enrichment analysis has been a successful combination for the identification of potent small molecules for the development of new drugs for cancer and virus infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a variety of medicinal chemistry strategies can be used for drug discovery.
a combination of HTS, medicinal chemistry and SEA can be used to identify potent inhibitors of proteins that are difficult to crystallize and/or are not amenable to biochemical assays.
medicinal chemistry can be used to accelerate the discovery of new drug candidates.
